label: thm:motivic-perpetual-obstruction
title: Motivic perpetual obstruction: $\chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A$ is non-trivial at almost every finite place when $\chi(A) \neq 0$
html:
We lift the Kummer-tower perpetuity result (Kummer tower) to a single algebraic statement at the level of the motivic Galois character.

Theorem (motivic perpetual obstruction) (proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)). Let A be a Frobenius–Hopf substrate with motivic class [A] \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} and motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A. If \chi(A) \neq 0, then \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is non-trivial at every finite place p of \mathbb{Q} with p \nmid \chi(A). Equivalently, the local Frobenius character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_{A, p} has a non-trivial element in

  H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p),\, \mu_n(1)\bigr)

for every n coprime to p\,\chi(A). The obstruction \kappa_0 projects to a non-trivial Frobenius character at every such place.

Sketch. We apply QU-to-QOU to identify \kappa_0 with the Euler class e(\xi) of the Reeb bundle, satisfying \langle e(\xi), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) (Poincaré–Hopf). Under the realization \rho_p \colon \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_{p^k}(q) (motivic substrate), the Euler class projects to a Frobenius character whose trace equals \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) \bmod p. Because p \nmid \chi(A), this trace is non-zero modulo p. The character is non-trivial. The class \kappa_0 retains a non-trivial Galois-cohomological component at every such place. By Hochschild–Kummer, gerbe non-vanishing in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) and Galois non-vanishing in H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}(\dots, \mu_n(1)) are HKR-equivalent. \square

Subsumption of prior arguments. This theorem subsumes every prior argument for the non-vanishing of \kappa_n in the brane tower. In particular:
